The wording about being an HKU student choosing “courses” before a deadline is a deliberate ambiguity. The “courses” were banquet dishes, not university classes. By the deadline, the student had chosen the menu for a banquet. When the banquet took place that evening, the selected courses were served; the student ate some of the dishes, discovered after tasting that some were disliked, and left those portions uneaten. The rejected or unfinished food was cleared away, and other dishes were consumed over the evening, so none of the chosen courses remained. Thus all the “courses” were gone in one evening because they were food courses served and cleared at a banquet, not academic courses lost from an enrollment system.
